title: 20.7 A 384-Site Chip Platform for Biochemical Applications with Individual Site Precision Temperature Control
problem: Biochemical processors require independent temperature control on multiple sites (384-site platform) for parallel PCR, gene assembly, and other thermally-tuned reactions, but silicon substrate thermal conductivity prevents efficient local isolation and precise sensing.
motivation: Scaling biochemical throughput requires multiple independent thermal zones in monolithic silicon without cross-talk, enabling simultaneous reactions at different temperatures.
method: 384-site chip platform using thermal isolation structures and independent local temperature sensors/heaters per site, overcoming substrate thermal conductivity to achieve precise individual-site temperature control for biochemical applications.
key_novelty: Monolithic 384-site platform with per-site independent temperature control achieved via substrate engineering to prevent thermal cross-talk.
contributions: 384 independently controllable temperature sites on single chip
Precision temperature control per biochemical reaction site
Thermal isolation structures enabling independent heating without cross-coupling
limitations: Specific temperature range, control precision, and response-time specifications not provided in abstract.
primary_theme: Multi-site biochemical processor with independent thermal zones.
